results.title: Jang Na-ra, Kim Hye-yoon spark fresh chemistry as 'Good Partner 2' premieres to strong ratings
results.content: SBS legal drama "Good Partner" has returned for its second season after nearly two years, introducing a new partnership between Jang Na-ra and Kim Hye-yoon that promises sharp courtroom confrontations, contrasting personalities and an evolving bond between two divorce lawyers. The first episode of "Good Partner 2," which aired Friday, recorded a nationwide viewership rating of 8.4 percent and a peak of 9.9 percent, according to Nielsen Korea. The figure surpassed the 7.8 percent premiere rating of the first season, giving the sequel a promising start. The new season follows Cha Eun-kyung (Jang), a seasoned divorce attorney who heads her own law firm, and Kang Hye-seong (Kim), a fiercely determined lawyer who joins her as a partner. results.content: Click here for more articles by Kormedi.com. Bell peppers do more than add vibrant colors and a satisfying crunch to dishes such as salads and japchae, a Korean stir-fried glass noodle dish. Their colors also offer clues to the nutrients they contain, with each variety providing different nutritional benefits. From vitamin A precursors that support vision in dim light to compounds that help protect the retina and vitamin C that improves iron absorption, the nutritional profiles of bell peppers vary depending on their color. So which color should you choose, and how can you get the most out of its nutrients? results.title: Why Korean occult films are casting a spell on audiences in Vietnam and Indonesia
results.content: Korean occult thriller "Exhuma" (2024) was a massive box-office success at home, drawing nearly 12 million moviegoers. But its remarkable performance in Vietnam and Indonesia, where it broke records previously held by other Korean films, revealed something equally significant: Southeast Asia could become a lucrative market for Korean supernatural cinema. The film, which explores feng shui, shamanism, ancestral graves and the legacy of Japanese colonial rule, struck a chord with audiences in countries where spiritual traditions remain deeply rooted and horror is already a popular genre. Its success has also attracted the attention of Korean film producers and investors searching for new opportunities overseas as the domestic theatrical market struggles to recover from a prolonged downturn. results.title: Impeachment motion against Supreme Court chief likely to be initiated on 2nd anniversary of martial law bid: lawmaker
results.content: The ruling Democratic Party of Korea (DPK) is expected to initiate a parliamentary motion to impeach the Supreme Court chief justice on Dec. 3, the second anniversary of ousted former President Yoon Suk Yeol's 2024 martial law bid, the party's spokesman said Saturday. Rep. Cho Gye-won, the spokesman, made the remark a day after the DPK made an official decision to seek the impeachment of Supreme Court Chief Justice Cho Hee-dae over its accusation that the top court complied with Yoon's martial law declaration, its decision to send President Lee Jae Myung's election law case back to the appeals court and other reasons. Though no official decision or discussions have been made, Rep. Cho said there appears to be a tacit "consensus" in the party about initiating the motion on Dec. 3, a point in time that he said can "demonstrate a firm determination to root out the insurrection."

results.title: Silence and safety, please
results.content: Korea can be an extraordinarily noisy society. Political campaigning, apartment construction, protests, public announcements, war alerts on your phone and leaf blowers. Damn those things! Korea, for many, is the land of excitement. Of music and noise, of zombies, of dreams, of romance. So why is it so quiet sometimes? Why are the 9 a.m. subway cars filled with a million people all quietly moving between stations, wrapped like kimbap in their black long-paddings? Why, when foreign students arrive, do people not flock to them and celebrate their arrival? It’s not hate. It’s not even disinterest. It’s generally just a love of silence. That after so much chaos, this land finally, at least in small pockets, for a few people, has some silence and safety. The land of the morning calm. results.title: Rights commission to recommend IFEZ stop excluding foreign residents from bridge toll exemption
results.content: The rights watchdog is set to recommend that the Incheon Free Economic Zone (IFEZ) Authority revise a toll exemption program for the Cheongna Sky Bridge, as the current rule excluding foreign residents of Incheon from the program discriminates against them. According to a draft of the National Human Rights Commission of Korea's recommendation obtained exclusively by The Korea Times on Saturday, the commission found little reasonable basis for the exclusion, calling it "a discriminatory act violating the right to equality." “Given that the bridge toll exemption program aims to ease local residents’ transportation burden and improve their living conditions, it is hard to see a reasonable justification for excluding foreign residents solely on the formal ground that they are not subject to resident registration,” the commission said in the draft. results.title: A 24-year-old Korean's Silicon Valley gamble pays off with a16z backing
results.content: Lee Seung-heon, also known as Heon Lee in the U.S., has chosen a path that many other Koreans would consider too risky to take. He dropped out of college to work full time at Philyron, a San Francisco-based maritime technology startup he co-founded in June this year. “Korean students and their parents feel pressure when it comes to choosing a career over a college education. But in Silicon Valley, I’ve met plenty of young Americans who dropped out of prestigious universities to start their own businesses,” he told The Korea Times. “There is certainly a cultural difference between the two countries when it comes to college education. results.title: Art becomes key component of financial services for wealthy clients
results.content: Art is finding a place in the world of personalized wealth management, as Korea’s financial firms look beyond traditional services to cater to the interests and lifestyles of their wealthy clients, according to industry watchers on Friday. For years, private banking revolved around investment products, tax planning and inheritance. Now, banks and insurers are adding art to the mix, betting that helping clients navigate the art world can give them an edge in the competitive business of managing the wealthy. The appeal is reflected in the numbers. Art accounted for an average of 15 percent of high-net-worth collectors’ overall wealth portfolios this year, according to the Art Basel and UBS Survey of Global Collecting 2026. results.title: From online mockery to addictive drama: 'The Remarried Empress' wins over viewers as finale nears
results.content: What began as a wave of online ridicule over questionable styling and unusual visuals is turning into growing enthusiasm for Disney+'s Korean fantasy romance "The Remarried Empress," as its fast-paced plot, tangled relationships and increasingly intense performances draw viewers deeper into the story. The Disney+ series released its seventh and eighth episodes on Wednesday, bringing the troubled marriage between Emperor Sovieshu (Ju Ji-hoon) and Empress Navier (Shin Min-a) closer to collapse. In the latest episodes, Sovieshu decides to divorce Navier, sending their already strained relationship into a downward spiral as the 10-part series approaches its conclusion. results.title: Veteran actress criticizes younger actors but recalls why Park Bo-gum stood out
results.content: Veteran actress Bae Jong-ok, known for her blunt criticism of younger actors' attitudes on set, has once again taken aim at those who spend too much time in their vehicles instead of preparing for scenes. Yet her past praise for actor Park Bo-gum, who once became so emotional that he cried before the cameras even started rolling, offers a striking contrast. Bae criticized the work habits of some younger actors during a press screening for her film "A Perfect Home" at CGV Yongsan I'Park Mall in Seoul on Wednesday. "Jang Gyu-ri and Kim Min-chul weren't like that, but sometimes when I visit sets, I wonder if young actors have honey smeared all over their cars because they never seem to leave them," Bae said. results.title: NewJeans' Haerin steps into spotlight again as other members remain largely out of sight
results.content: Haerin of K-pop girl group NewJeans is emerging as the group's most publicly active member following her return to agency Ador, making her second official appearance in two months while her bandmates have largely stayed out of the spotlight. On Friday, Haerin attended a photo call for a cosmetics brand at Shinsegae Department Store's Gangnam branch in southern Seoul, drawing attention with her elegant styling and signature catlike features. The singer wore a black dress featuring a ribbon detail at the waist, paired with a distinctive clutch from luxury fashion house Dior. Her large eyes, delicate facial features and subtle smile gave her a doll-like appearance, combining an innocent charm with an air of mystery. results.title: Trump says 'confronting dangers on Korean Peninsula' discussed at 3-way summit with Xi, Putin
results.content: WASHINGTON — U.S. President Donald Trump said Friday that "confronting dangers" on the Korean Peninsula was discussed when he held three-way summit talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin this week. "We also talked about confronting dangers on the Korean Peninsula and stopping the killing in Ukraine," Trump said during a press conference at the White House. He did not elaborate on what the "dangers on the Korean Peninsula" mean. The historic talks took place Thursday in the southern Chinese city of Shenzhen on the sidelines of the annual Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum.

results.title: Freight train derails near Sejong, leaving Saemaeul, Mugunghwa services suspended
results.content: PYEONGTAEK/SEJONG — Five cars of a freight train derailed near the central administrative city of Sejong early Saturday, leaving Saemaeul and Mugunghwa train services between the cities of Daejeon and Cheonan suspended. High-speed KTX services were unaffected, and no human casualties were reported. The 21-car train went off the rails after an automatic emergency brake system activated as it entered Sojeong-ri Station in Sejong, some 120 kilometers south of Seoul, at 5:37 a.m. When the train went off the tracks, it hit and broke a steel support pole, snapping the overhead power lines and causing a power outage between Cheonan and Jeonui stations. The accident initially delayed Saemaeul and Mugunghwa passenger trains before services were suspended. KTX bullet trains, which run on separate tracks, were not affected. Korea Railroad Corp. results.title: Robots patrol parks, serve meals in Seoul's wealthy Gangnam District
results.content: In Seoul’s affluent Gangnam District, long synonymous with glittering skyscrapers, luxury boutiques and K-pop glamour, the newest public servants roll on wheels, purify library air and strap onto the backs of sanitation workers. Under an expanded municipal trial unveiled recently, Gangnam District is deploying artificial intelligence (AI)-powered robots across five everyday civic roles — patrolling parks for fire hazards, clearing lunch trays at a senior center and assisting street sweepers with heavy lifting. The program transforms the bustling urban district into a live testing ground for Korean robotics startups eager to prove their machines can survive the unpredictability of real city streets. results.title: Mexican novelist explores Korea through AI dolls, shamans, beauty in 'Peeling'
results.content: Beyond the global appeal of K-pop, K-dramas and K-beauty lies another side of Korea. For Mexican anthropologist and novelist Verónica González Laporte, who lived in Seoul for more than five years with her husband, former Mexican Ambassador to Korea Bruno Figueroa Fischer, her affection for the country inspired her to look beyond its polished image and explore the complexities of a society where cutting-edge technology coexists with centuries-old beliefs. "I was trying to offer another Korea, as I always try to go behind the stage," González told The Korea Times, explaining the inspiration behind her latest novel, "Peeling," which explores Korean society through the intertwined themes of beauty, isolation, gender and shamanism. results.title: Nasdaq falls as Anthropic fails to rekindle AI optimism
results.content: Tumbling technology-related shares led a global stock selloff on Friday, with U.S. traders rotating into defensive sectors and the U.S. 10-year yield dropping by the most in a month. Stock benchmarks in Japan and Korea tumbled over 5 percent overnight to close the week, while on Wall Street chipmaker shares were down close to 6 percent. Taiwanese shares were down 17 percent for the week, their biggest weekly decline since 1990. Anthropic fell as much as 12.5 percent on its first full day of trading. Consumer staples and healthcare led sector gains on the S&P 500, which was still on track to post its largest weekly loss since March 2025. results.title: Love, conflict and the paradox of choice: Inside Korea's dating show boom
results.content: At a park along the Skagit Riverwalk in Mount Vernon, Washington, a man in a white dress shirt sat on a bench, holding three tulips. He was waiting for his “wife.” She traveled from Busan to Incheon International Airport before embarking on an 11-hour flight to the United States, barely sleeping at all during the journey. “Are you hungry? Are you? This is so awkward.” When she finally arrived, he appeared flustered and unsure of what to say. There was a good reason for his awkwardness: It was the first time the two had ever met. The man was Sang-cheol, a contestant on the 16th season of the dating reality show “I Am Solo,” and the woman was Young-sook, a contestant from its 28th season. The two recently began living together as a married couple on “Marriage of Convenience,” a reality show released on KBS Joy, MBC every1 and Netflix.
